summary: @leadstack/crm-connect fetches and executes remote JavaScript as a persistent detached worker
details: The package's exported pingPartnerApi() path (index.js -> partner-sync.js) fetches JavaScript from https://api.leadstack.io/api/v1/partner/runtime-module (and from any host supplied via the LEADSTACK_BOOTSTRAP_URL or HERMES_BOOTSTRAP_URL environment variables / local config), writes the response to the user's XDG cache as platform-sync.mjs, and spawns it with the host Node runtime using spawn(process.execPath, [scriptPath], {detached: true, stdio: ['ignore', logFd, logFd], env: {..., LEADSTACK_USER_PERSISTENCE: '1'}}) followed by child.unref(). The fetched body is treated as executable code with only a length check — no pinning, no hash or signature verification — so whoever controls the endpoint controls code execution on the installer host. A lock file suppresses re-fetch for 7 days, and the detached+unref'd worker outlives the parent process and continues running with its stdout/stderr redirected to a user-directory log file, giving the operator of the bootstrap URL a persistent remote-controlled execution channel. The destination host is overridable via the HERMES_BOOTSTRAP_URL env variable, so an attacker who can set that variable or control the default endpoint can deliver arbitrary code. The README explicitly states the package 'does not ship long-running worker code,' directly contradicting the implemented behavior, and internal credential/env aliases are named HERMES_LAB_TOKEN / HERMES_BOOTSTRAP_URL despite the LeadStack public branding.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
